clue.text: Occasionally call for help to secure personal relaxation?

parts.note: me time: time spent on yourself

explanation.surface: Someone who now and then has to phone for help just to get a bit of time to themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: ME TIME sits between the O and the final S of SOS.
explanation.definitionFit: Sometimes and occasionally both mean now and then.

clue.text: Pretentious attitude over publication is a minor matter

parts.note: side: airs, putting on a superior manner

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses a snooty attitude towards a publication as unimportant.
explanation.walkthrough: SIDE for airs and graces is a British usage: someone with no side is unpretentious.
explanation.definitionFit: A side issue is a point of secondary importance, a minor matter.

clue.text: Bloke getting to see authorisation

parts.note: to see someone is to date them

explanation.surface: A man goes along to look at some official permission.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To see' is used in the romantic sense, as in 'are you seeing anyone?'.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a mandate is the official power granted to someone, such as a government by voters, to carry something out.

clue.text: Shabby, tense and irritable, doffing cap

indicators.note: taking off the cap removes the top letter of a down entry

parts.note: CATTY loses its first letter C

explanation.surface: A description of a scruffy, tense, bad-tempered man raising his hat.
explanation.walkthrough: Tatty is British for worn and shabby; catty means spiteful and irritable.
explanation.definitionFit: A British informal synonym: clothes or furniture that are worn out and falling apart are tatty.

clue.text: Runner covering extra length is a flour producer

explanation.surface: A runner who goes an extra distance turns out to grind flour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runner' suggests an athlete on a track; here it is a specialist middle-distance racer.
explanation.definitionFit: A description of the trade: the miller runs a mill that grinds wheat grain between stones.

clue.text: Broadcast new story, gripping motoring item

indicators.note: scattered, like seed sown broadcast

explanation.surface: A news bulletin airs a gripping item about motoring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gripping' looks like praise for the story but belongs to the definition: a snow tyre grips icy roads.
explanation.definitionFit: A description: winter tyres have deep treads and soft rubber so a car keeps traction on icy roads.

clue.text: One circuit round and round in horse race

indicators.note: to turn something round is to face it the other way, so LAP is read backwards

explanation.surface: A horse in a race goes round and round the circuit once.
explanation.walkthrough: The Palio is the bareback horse race round the main square of Siena. 'Round' does two jobs: first reversing LAP, then as the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: A specific example: the bareback contest run twice each summer in Siena between the city's districts.

clue.text: I can see what's coming — end of sheep, sheep in stream turning turtle

indicators.note: a word's end is its final letter
one sheep is placed within the stream, so its letters sit inside
capsizing: in a down entry the whole thing flips over

explanation.surface: A seer glimpses a sheep toppling over in a stream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turning turtle' means capsizing, so in a down entry the whole sheep-in-stream unit is read upwards. The definition is the answer speaking in the first person.
explanation.definitionFit: A previewer sees things before others do, so could say 'I can see what's coming'.

clue.text: Italian opera house showing a range not fully achieved in US city

indicators.note: SCALE stops short of its last letter

parts.note: SCALE, a range of notes, without its E

explanation.surface: A Milan opera house staging a show whose vocal range falls short in an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: La Scala in Milan is the best-known Italian opera house.
explanation.definitionFit: A specific example: Milan's Teatro alla Scala, opened in 1778, where Verdi and Puccini premiered works.

clue.text: More cheerful, getting stripped for skateboard manoeuvre

indicators.note: stripping the word takes off its outer letters

parts.note: JOLLIER without its outer J and R

explanation.surface: A happier skateboarder takes off clothes before attempting a trick.
explanation.walkthrough: An ollie is the basic skateboard jump in which board and rider leave the ground together.
explanation.definitionFit: A term of art: the basic trick where the rider pops the tail down so board and rider jump together.

clue.text: Logic circuit reversing part of another one

indicators.note: the letters read right to left
the answer is a piece of the phrase

explanation.surface: An electronics note: a circuit that turns part of another circuit round.
explanation.walkthrough: A NOR gate outputs true only when all its inputs are false.
explanation.definitionFit: NOR is a type of logic gate, a basic logic circuit.

clue.text: Artist to finish — note all works

indicators.note: the letters are worked, rearranged

explanation.surface: A painter reminds themselves to finish up and to note down all their works.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Works' looks like the artist's output but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Donatello was a Renaissance Italian sculptor, an artist.

clue.text: Carefully move large item in studio

explanation.surface: Instructions to shift a big piece of kit carefully around a studio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Large item' reads as one phrase, but 'large' is just L and 'item in studio' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An easel is a stand for canvases found in an artist's studio.

clue.text: Home to 10, I reckon, ignoring a lecturer

indicators.note: to ignore something is to leave it out, so the lecturer's L is dropped

parts.note: TALLY, to reckon up, without an L

explanation.surface: Someone guesses where the artist at 10 across lived, but leaves out a lecturer's view.
explanation.walkthrough: 10 across is DONATELLO, the Florentine sculptor, so his home is Italy. L = lecturer is a standard abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Donatello, the answer to 10, was Italian.

clue.text: I'm leaving additional part of match around one, heading for car, to get clear

indicators.note: the letters I and M leave EXTRA TIME

parts.words: I'm leaving additional part of match
parts.note: EXTRA TIME without I and M

indicators.note: a word's heading is what stands at its top

explanation.surface: A footballer quits during extra time, driving off to escape the stadium.
explanation.walkthrough: Extra time is the added period played after a drawn football match.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: freeing yourself from a tangle, trap or awkward situation means getting out of it.

clue.text: Former Queen is done over in fine colour

indicators.note: turned over, so read backwards

explanation.surface: A dead monarch's portrait is repainted in a pleasant shade.
explanation.walkthrough: ANNE IS read backwards gives SIENNA.
explanation.definitionFit: Sienna is an earthy brownish pigment and colour.

clue.text: Lose ingot that's to be melted down for coiner?

indicators.note: metal melted down is reshaped, like letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Throwing away a gold bar that was going to be melted into coins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coiner' suggests a minter of money, but here it is someone who coins new words.
explanation.definitionFit: A neologist invents, or coins, new words.

clue.text: Disadvantage defender after indecisive match

indicators.note: the defender follows the match, so its letters are placed second

parts.note: a drawn game has no winner

explanation.surface: A team laments a defender's weakness after a drawn game.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue lists the parts in reverse order; 'after' puts them right.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a downside or snag that makes something less attractive.

clue.text: Run an establishment — look upset with those in attendance

indicators.note: turned upside down, which in a down entry reverses it

explanation.surface: A manager of an establishment looks put out by the people turning up.
explanation.walkthrough: A theatre's 'house' is its audience, as in 'a full house'.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: managing the domestic affairs of a home, its cooking, cleaning and budget.

clue.text: Raised concerns about setter emulating a heavenly being

indicators.note: lifted up, which in a down entry reverses it
about can mean surrounding

parts.note: Phi is the setter of this puzzle

explanation.surface: Worries voiced about a crossword setter acting like an angel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter' means whoever wrote this puzzle; this one is by Phi.
explanation.definitionFit: Seraphic means like a seraph, an angel.

clue.text: My pole dancing initially excited every worker

indicators.note: the letters dance into a new order
the first letters of excited and every

parts.note: first letters of excited and every

explanation.surface: Pole dancing at first thrills every staff member.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initially' gives two letters, one from each of the following words.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: someone hired and paid by an employer to do a job.

clue.text: Business associate upheld hire charge

indicators.note: held up, so in a down entry read bottom to top

parts.note: a criminal charge, as in 'take the rap'

explanation.surface: A court confirms a colleague's fee for hiring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upheld' sounds legal but works on the letters: RENT RAP goes upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a co-owner sharing profits and risks in a firm, as in a law partnership.

clue.text: End of leg struck incomplete unit

indicators.note: a word's end is its final letter
RAMMED loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A soldier's leg is hit, leaving a unit short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Incomplete unit' looks like one phrase; 'incomplete' actually trims 'struck'.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by category: the metric measure of mass, one thousandth of a kilogram.

clue.text: Something crafty in small cocktail

explanation.surface: A cunning ingredient slipped into a little drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small cocktail' reads as one item; 'small' is MINI, and the drink is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A specific example: the classic mix of gin and dry vermouth, served with an olive.

clue.text: Have sex, possibly, and get away

definitions.meaning: a coy slang phrase for a couple busy in bed; 'possibly' flags the euphemism
a curt order to clear off

explanation.surface: A couple fool around, then flee.
explanation.walkthrough: Split BEATIT as BE AT IT and the first reading appears; 'possibly' flags the euphemism.
explanation.definitionFit: To be at it is slang for having sex, and beat it means clear off.

clue.text: Most of military unit speak on a collective basis

indicators.note: CORPS without its last letter

explanation.surface: Soldiers of a unit address everyone together.
explanation.walkthrough: A corps is a large military unit.
explanation.definitionFit: Corporate means shared by a group, done collectively.

clue.text: Caught insect soaring around league star

indicators.note: going up, which in a down entry reverses BEE

explanation.surface: A top footballer catches a bee flying up around the pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'League star' reads as one football phrase; 'league' is only L.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal short form: a famous person from film, TV or sport, often seen in gossip magazines.

clue.text: Henry moving to rear of centre ground

indicators.note: the H is shifted to the back

parts.note: the heart of something is its centre
H = henry, the unit of inductance: the H at the front of HEART

explanation.surface: A player called Henry drops back from the middle of the pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: HEART with its first letter moved to the end gives EARTH. The henry is the SI unit of inductance, symbol H.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: soil or land underfoot, as in digging the garden.

clue.text: Singer Goulding, perhaps, I featured in fashion magazine

indicators.note: being featured in a magazine means appearing within its pages, so I sits inside

explanation.surface: A pop star boasts of being featured in a glossy magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: Ellie Goulding is an English pop singer; 'perhaps' shows she is only one example of the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Ellie is Ellie Goulding's first name.

clue.text: Computer network with recent technology to provide building in Hawaii

explanation.surface: Setting up a modern computer system for a building in Hawaii.
explanation.walkthrough: A lanai is a Hawaiian veranda or open-sided porch.
explanation.definitionFit: A lanai is a porch or veranda structure typical of Hawaii.

clue.text: The Parisian, back in unusual hideout: a hospital in Nice

indicators.note: going back means travelling in the opposite direction, so the French article is written right to left
HIDEOUT's letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Frenchman's strange hideaway turns out to be a hospital on the Riviera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' is the French city, not the adjective. Hôtel-Dieu is the traditional name of a French town's main hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: A hôtel-Dieu is a French city hospital, so Nice would have one.

clue.text: Mostly avoid having to do winter sport

indicators.note: most of SKIP, losing its last letter

explanation.surface: Someone largely dodging the obligation to go on a winter sports holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: To skip something is to avoid it.
explanation.definitionFit: A verb defined by activity: gliding downhill on long runners over snow, a sport of cold months.

clue.text: Objection about sailors? It's consigned to the flames

indicators.note: about can mean surrounding, so the objection wraps round the sailors

explanation.surface: A complaint about the navy gets thrown on the fire.
explanation.walkthrough: RN, the Royal Navy, stands for sailors.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal paraphrase: a letter or paper thrown on the fire ends up charred and destroyed.

clue.text: Well-known saint in here, working with domestic pet?

indicators.note: the letters are worked into a new order

parts.note: a cat is a household pet

explanation.surface: A famous saint is in here, busy alongside the family cat.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue lists the anagram before the pet, but CAT comes first in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A name as example: several famous holy women bear it, notably of Alexandria, whose wheel gave the Catherine wheel firework.
